about: GENERATED by tools/spec-tree.js from the government documents (sources/, tools/spec-read.js) and sources/hand-maths.json — never edit by hand (a hand edit fails the build). A node per heading and per statement, named as printed. THE @FAMILY MATHS TOPIC TREE, FROM THE GOVERNMENT'S OWN LISTS (owner, 24–25 Nov: the library's one source of truth is the UK government spec). Strand › topic › sub-topic, each node an id, a short plain name (paraphrased, never copied), its source lines in the DfE documents (`src`: doc + the section heading exactly as printed, one of headings.json, or GCSE statement code) and, for a sub-topic, the levels it is taught at (KS1, KS2, KS3; GCSE Foundation and Higher, Higher only where the GCSE document prints the content in bold). A maths question's `dfe` (data/questions.json) is the node(s) it tests, read by tools/lib/curriculum.js from the country files only: `ideas` (its idea_id, the 24 Nov idea tree of data/settings/question-ideas.json, mapped onto this tree), its AQA 8300 `spec_ref` (AQA numbers its points as the DfE GCSE statements), `set` and `topic` (a source's own topic name). `gen_ideas`: the maths idea a generated @family set (tools/lib/qgen.js) under a sub-topic no idea of `ideas` maps to reads as its idea, the card that teaches it — a node with an idea of its own never borrows one. Find's topic question answers a maths question's nodes broad → narrow. A worksheet's name is its `worksheet`, never a topic. Checked by tools/one-curriculum.js. `statements`: the GCSE statement codes (a spec point aqa-8300:N2 is GCSE N2). `doc_url`: every document is on gov.uk. `gen`: the generated sets and rows keep their first ids (tools/lib/qgen.js); `level` the levels a templated sub-topic must be taught at, in order, and `tiers` the set tier of each (a Higher-only sub-topic makes a Higher set). `templates`: sub-topic -> skill ids of data/settings/qgen.json. `budget`: maths questions with no node (A-Level and mechanics, outside these documents; Corbettmaths 5-a-day rows with no topic; problem-solving sets), may only fall.
